meta.case_name: Save the job of an INSEAD alumnus!

prompt.context: Your client 'Techking' is a 5 billion euro multi-national IT provider based in Germany that provides technology and related consulting services to clients from a variety of industries. Revenues have been next to stagnant for years and profit margins compared to competitors are low. The CEO — an INSEAD alumnus — has asked you to come up with options on how to turnaround their business and improve profit margins. He advised you that all previous consulting companies were 'not bold enough' and this is the time for some 'big changes', as he otherwise will lose his job.
prompt.question: How would you turnaround Techking's business and improve profit margins? The CEO is looking for bold options, not incremental fixes.

clarifying_info.q: What does Techking's product/service portfolio look like?
clarifying_info.a: The client's offerings include a wide range of technologies including provision of computing power from data centers, hardware for employees (e.g. laptops), software, and consulting services.
The client operates all over the world, but the focus is Europe (>50 countries).

clarifying_info.q: Has the client already tried to cut costs?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the client has already executed several smaller initiatives to cut down costs, but the impact was minimal.

clarifying_info.q: What is the target profitability and timeline?
clarifying_info.a: The client targets at least 15% profitability in 3 years at the latest and would accept a cut in revenue if necessary. Current profitability has to be calculated from the data.
Profit margins of competitors are between 15% and 25%.

clarifying_info.q: Is the client open to M&A?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the client is open to M&A activities.

clarifying_info.q: Are competitors facing the same low-growth issues?
clarifying_info.a: No, competitors are not facing the same issues.
Techking is a trusted German brand, but the client is not seen as innovative and has not managed to turnaround the business on their own. The product portfolio was developed in-house.

clarifying_info.q: Is the client's performance significantly different across markets?
clarifying_info.a: No, performance is not significantly different across markets.

exhibits.title: Annual revenues and CAGR — Top 5 competitors (in bn €)
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing annual global revenues (in bn €) and CAGR for Techking and four named competitors: Miracle, Tech & Co., Matec, and Neologic.

exhibits.title: M&A activities (acquisitions) in last three years
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the number of acquisitions made in the last three years by Techking and each of its four named competitors.

exhibits.title: Profitability, revenue growth, and revenue share per product segment
exhibits.shows: A 2x2 scatter plot with Revenue Growth (CAGR) on the x-axis and Profit Margin (%) on the y-axis. Four product segments (A: Workplace, B: Software, C: Consulting, D: Cybersecurity) are plotted. Revenue share per segment is also shown: A 30%, B 30%, C 25%, D 15%.

framework: Profitability tree: Revenue (price x volume) vs. Costs (variable + fixed) to identify the gap vs. 15% target
Benchmark vs. competition: Revenue size, growth rates (CAGR), M&A activity — where is Techking falling behind?
Product portfolio analysis: Break profitability and growth by segment to find drag vs. value
Strategic options generation: At least two bold options (divest, double-down via M&A, cost restructuring)
Feasibility and risk assessment: For each option, identify major risks and rough implementation considerations
Recommendation: Combine options with clear pros/cons, link to achieving 15% margin in 3 years

questions.prompt: Calculate Techking's current overall profit margin and profit in absolute terms.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 3 data to compute segment-level profits and sum them. Total revenue is 5 bn €. Current overall margin is ~8%, which is well below the 15% target and below competitor range of 15-25%.

math.setup: Revenue 5 bn €; segments: A=1.5 bn @ -20%, B=1.5 bn @ 5%, C=1.25 bn @ 25%, D=0.75 bn @ 40%
math.answer: Total profit ~375 m€; overall margin ~7.5–8%, significantly below the 15% target.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell you about Techking's competitive position on growth?
questions.guidance: Techking's CAGR of 3% is far below every competitor. Three competitors have revenues 4–5x larger, suggesting significant scale disadvantages. The market is fragmented with many smaller players as well.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 2 tell you about the relationship between M&A and growth?
questions.guidance: There is a clear positive correlation between number of acquisitions and revenue CAGR. Matec (33 acquisitions, 31% CAGR) and Tech & Co. (21 acquisitions, 17% CAGR) are the clearest examples. Techking has made zero acquisitions and has the lowest CAGR. Candidate should identify that the absence of M&A may have structurally held back Techking.

questions.prompt: What strategic options would you recommend to achieve 15% profitability within 3 years? Walk through at least two bold options.
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers at minimum: (A) Divest segment A (Workplace) — loss-making at -20% margin, 30% of revenue; this would raise margin significantly. (B) Double down on high-margin segments C and D via acquisitions. (C) Aggressive cost restructuring. Great answer analyzes multiple options with pros, cons, and risks, and estimates resulting margin for each.

math.setup: Option A: Divest Workplace segment (1.5 bn € revenue, -300 m€ profit). Post-divestiture: revenue = 3.5 bn €, profit = 375 + 300 = 675 m€.
steps: New revenue after divesting A: 5 bn − 1.5 bn = 3.5 bn €
New total profit: 375 m€ + 300 m€ (no longer losing) = 675 m€
math.answer: Divesting Workplace segment alone brings margin to ~19%, exceeding the 15% target and saving the CEO's job.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the key non-financial considerations and risks the client should assess before pursuing the recommended options?

categories.name: M&A execution risks
ideas: Techking has no M&A track record — cultural integration could fail
Overpaying for acquisitions in hot segments like cybersecurity
Management bandwidth and capability to integrate acquired entities
Regulatory approval may be required for large acquisitions

categories.name: Divestiture risks
ideas: Finding a buyer for a loss-making Workplace segment may be difficult or time-consuming
Workforce reductions may cause reputational damage and employee morale issues
Existing clients may have bundled contracts spanning multiple segments
Revenue drop from 5 bn to 3.5 bn may alarm investors or creditors short-term

categories.name: Competitive and market risks
ideas: Cybersecurity and consulting markets are increasingly competitive
If Techking waits too long, best M&A targets may be acquired by competitors
German brand trust advantage may not translate in non-European markets

categories.name: Implementation and timing risks
ideas: Three-year deadline is tight for a full turnaround including M&A
Previous cost-cutting initiatives failed — cultural resistance to change
Board and shareholder alignment required for bold structural moves

recommendation: Divest product segment A (Workplace) as the immediate priority: it is loss-making at -20% margin and represents 30% of revenues; divestiture eliminates -300 m€ drag and brings overall margin to ~19%, exceeding the 15% target

Pursue acquisitions in high-margin segments C (Consulting) and D (Cybersecurity) to drive revenue growth and scale, leveraging competitors' evidence that M&A is the primary driver of growth in this market
Conduct a review of segment B (Software) — currently at only 5% margin — for restructuring or partial divestiture to further improve profitability
If M&A is the chosen growth path, build internal M&A capability immediately (integration team, deal sourcing) given Techking has zero experience
risks: No M&A track record increases integration risk significantly
Divesting 30% of revenue reduces scale and may trigger client or investor concern in the short term
Cybersecurity M&A targets may be expensive given market demand
Timeline of 3 years is aggressive for both a divestiture and acquisitions to close and integrate
next_steps: Commission a detailed valuation and buyer search for Workplace segment within 90 days
Identify 3–5 acquisition targets in Consulting and Cybersecurity and assess strategic fit
Build an internal M&A integration team or hire external M&A advisory
Define KPIs for each initiative with quarterly milestones to track progress toward the 15% margin target
